newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Arenaturist sees mln mark pre-tax in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Arenaturist sees mln mark pre-tax in 1997.

text.p: Croatian Adriatic seaside hotelier Arenaturist said on Wednesday it expected one million German marks pre-tax profit this year on planned income of 44 million marks as the tourist trade recovered.
"This year should be better than last year. We had a tiny profit in 1996, not really worth mentioning," deputy chief executive Milena Perkovic told Reuters by telephone.
Perkovic put 1996 income at 38 million marks, adding that most had been consumed by costs. With high bank lending rates, the cost of financing was particularly heavy, she said.
But 1996 still marked a turnaround for Arenaturist, based in Pula on the Istrian peninsula, after several meagre war years when very few foreign visitors ventured into Croatia.

The company hopes business will pick up further this year to produce a 30-percent increase in overnights to 1.7 million, Perkovic said and added: "The price of capital is lower, that should also help."
Arenaturist has nine hotels, seven camping sites, two apartment complexes and other facilities dispersed over 190 km of coastline.

Arenaturist's 218.25 million marks equity is divided into shares with a face value of 100 marks. The government recently earmarked almost 39 percent from its portfolio for mass privatisation through vouchers.
Private shareholders now have 43 percent in the company and Istarska Banka 14 percent. Some 3.4 percent is reserved for restitution to pre-World War Two owners of some facilities.
The company's stock fetched 150 kuna on Tuesday on an over-the-counter market, but has not been traded on Zagreb's bourse since late in February.
